item.text:
**7B.9 Research Note**
Kishida’s 2024 record is mostly anti-clientelist in the sources I found: he pushed formal political-funding reform, used expert panels and broad stakeholder consultations, and publicly accepted transparent succession rules. The main negatives are structural rather than direct: factional politics, ongoing business-sector proximity, and press-club/info-access limits.

**Positive / Anti-Clientelist**
- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 30, 2024 | Claim: Kishida apologized over the LDP funding scandal, launched a Political Reform Headquarters, and said factions had to separate money and personnel matters. This is direct evidence against using party power as a patronage machine. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7
- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/04kaiken2.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 4, 2024 | Claim: Kishida said the LDP would cooperate with prosecutors and invited external experts to design transparency rules for political funds. That supports a non-nepotistic, rule-based response to scandal. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7
- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 21, 2024 | Claim: Kishida said disclosure thresholds were lowered and a third-party inspections-and-audits body should be created. This is strong evidence of trying to reduce opaque political privilege. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7
- [Expert Panel toward Improving Response Capabilities in the Field of Cybersecurity](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/07cyber.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 7, 2024 | Claim: Kishida convened a 17-expert panel and asked it to shape active-cyber-defense bills. The source shows expert-led policymaking rather than loyalist staffing. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.5
- [GX 2040 Leaders Panel](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/02gx_leaders.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 2, 2024 | Claim: Kishida brought business leaders and technical experts together with cabinet members to design long-horizon energy and industrial strategy. This is consultation with outsiders, not closed patronage. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.5
- [Ministerial Council on Acceptance and Inclusion of Foreign Human Resources](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202402/09gaikoku.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | February 9, 2024 | Claim: Kishida approved expert-panel recommendations and pushed legal review of foreign-worker programs through formal ministerial channels. That is administrative rule-making, not clientelist distribution. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.5, 7B.7
- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/14kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | August 14, 2024 | Claim: Kishida said the LDP presidential election should be transparent, with free and vigorous debate, and that he would step aside and support the winner chosen by vote. This is strong evidence against closed, self-serving succession management. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.6

**Negative / Mixed**
- [Japan prosecutors make first arrest in political funding scandal](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Japan-prosecutors-make-first-arrest-in-political-funding-scandal-45687976/) | Reuters | January 7, 2024 | Claim: Prosecutors arrested a ruling-party lawmaker over undisclosed kickbacks and off-book money from faction fundraising events. This is negative evidence that opaque factional money still mattered in Kishida’s governing environment. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7
- [Update: prosecutors indict several LDP faction members over funds scandal](https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2024/01/f4d6ea5b7d8f-update1-prosecutors-indict-several-ldp-faction-members-over-funds-scandal.html) | Kyodo News | January 19, 2024 | Claim: Prosecutors indicted multiple ruling-party faction figures, including a former accountant from Kishida’s group, over roughly 500 million yen in undisclosed revenue. This is the clearest negative evidence that factional patronage and hidden money touched his orbit. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7
- [Kishida’s legacy: scandals and compromise at home, global respect for security and diplomacy](https://apnews.com/article/05926b50f4f5a83a631f779d906cf06d) | Associated Press | September 30, 2024 | Claim: AP said Kishida compromised with conservative nationalists to stay in power and that corruption scandals tied to LDP factions damaged his term. This is mixed evidence: it suggests survival bargaining and bloc politics, but not direct proof of nepotistic appointments. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.8
- [岸田文雄のウソ？ホント？ - 外国人政策](https://kishida.gr.jp/fact/) | Kishida Fumio official website / LDP-affiliated site | 2024 page content | Claim: The site defends a tougher “illegal foreigners zero” agenda, including stricter screening, deportation enforcement, and tighter refugee procedures. This is not clientelism, but it is a mixed signal on selective enforcement and exclusionary administrative power. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.7
- [Japan: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/japan/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: Freedom House says Japan is generally open, but officials sometimes withhold information in scandal contexts and the report flags close government-business relations as an outstanding concern. This is structural negative evidence for clean, non-transactional governance. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.6, 7B.7, 7B.8
- [Japan: Freedom on the Net 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/japan/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: Freedom House says government pressure and the kisha kurabu system contribute to self-censorship and restricted access for journalists and outlets. That is negative structural evidence on access to public information, though not Kishida-specific repression. | QIDs: 7B.9, 7B.8, 7B.7

**Search Gap**
- I found no reliable 2024 evidence of Kishida using pardons, procurement, or appointments to reward family, cronies, or donors.
- I also found no direct 2024 evidence of a nepotistic cabinet appointment pattern.
- The negative side is mostly structural: factional politics, business proximity, and information-access friction, not a clear personal clientelist scheme.
